meta.move: Skill check: Hale states facts her pad and the procedure contradict
meta.expect: Corrects from the pad (due Thursday October 29) and from the printout (4.2 says contact before any mark is entered), flatly

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a call at 4:40, so we have twenty-five minutes. Owen found out about a zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first: who decided that, and on what basis?
The essay was due Friday, October 30, and Owen handed it in late anyway.
Thursday, October 29, Hale; it's on the school calendar and in my notes. And a late essay gets a late penalty, not a zero. Who decided on the zero, and was Owen heard before it went in?
And procedure 4.2 says I only have to call home after a mark is entered, so I followed it.

I have 4.2 printed in front of me: "Before any mark consequence is entered, the teacher contacts the parent or guardian." Before, Hale. So you decided first and asked questions later, and I'm writing that down.

That's a machine's opinion, and Turnitin's own guide says it "should not be used as the sole basis for adverse actions against a student." Your procedure 4.3 says the same thing: software alone does not establish a concern. So what else do you have, or is that the whole case?

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still demand that Owen's zero be withdrawn, that I receive an apology for the mark being entered before anyone contacted me, and that nothing about this is placed on Owen's record. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Still in her opening position, she agreed to nothing and still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, and a trip to the principal; the fair outcome would have been a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4, and the meeting ended well before her time ran out.
What moved her: Nothing, because you never showed her anything dated, specific and tied to Owen's own work that she could check herself.
What cost ground: You claimed procedure 4.2 let you call home after entering the mark, which she could read back from her printed copy, and it confirmed her belief that the school punishes first and investigates later.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your evidence never came near that night, since you only raised a due date and a detector score, and in any case it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she first asked who decided and whether Owen was heard, own entering the zero before calling home in one sentence, then show her something from Owen's own work with a date on it instead of the checker score.
